title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 5th District
area: Parts of Philadelphia and Delaware County.

context.text: Mary Gay Scanlon advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. Nick Manganaro won the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Mary Gay Scanlon is the Democratic incumbent, in the U.S. House since a November 2018 special election. A lawyer who worked in legal-aid and child-advocacy roles and later directed pro bono programs at a national law firm, she also served as president of her local school board. She serves on the Judiciary and Rules committees.

background.text: Born in Syracuse, New York, in 1959.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Colgate University (1980) and a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School (1984).
Worked as a law clerk and as an attorney at Ballard Spahr, the Education Law Center of Pennsylvania and the Support Center for Child Advocates.

Her official biography says she was national pro bono counsel at a major U.S. law firm, where she directed and supervised over 600 lawyers in 15 offices providing more than 50,000 hours of pro bono legal services annually.
Before Congress, served as president of her local school board and co-chair of the Voting Rights Task Force of the Association of Pro Bono Counsel.
Sworn into the U.S. House on November 13, 2018, following a special election, and represents Pennsylvania's 5th District.

Serves on the House Committee on Rules and the Judiciary Committee, where she is ranking member of the Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee; also chairs the House Caucuses on Access to Legal Aid, Youth Mentoring, and Foster Youth.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), Ballotpedia lists her Judiciary subcommittees as Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and The Constitution and Limited Government, and the Rules Subcommittee on Rules and Organization of the House.
Lives in Swarthmore with her husband, Mark; they have three adult children, according to her official biography.

record.text: Was ranking member of the Judiciary Committee's Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Serves on the Judiciary Committee's Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement Subcommittee in the 119th Congress.
Serves on the House Rules Committee, which sets the terms of debate for legislation on the House floor, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Nick Manganaro
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Nick Manganaro is a retired financial professional and former Republican precinct committeeman who has lived in the 5th District for more than 25 years. He describes himself as running against policies he says harm the district's citizens and favors fiscal discipline and limited government.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, grew up in Chester County, just outside what is now the 5th District, and has lived in the district for more than 25 years.
Graduated from the Episcopal Academy, earned a bachelor's degree from Reed College (1979) and a graduate degree from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1984).

Spent most of his career in the finance industry, in research, product development, and risk management, consulting with multi-national financial firms on quantifying and managing risk; Ballotpedia lists his work as investor.
A former Republican precinct committeeman and now retired.
Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the 5th District unopposed on the ballot (25,075 votes); endorsed by the Delaware County GOP and Pennsylvania Young Republicans.

priorities.text: Says federal debt is growing faster than the economy and is unsustainable, and calls for fiscal discipline and holding the line on government spending rather than expanding the social safety net.
priorities.quote: The Federal debt is too darn high because members of Congress have a hard time making decisions and just saying no sometimes. Federal debt is growing faster than the economy as a whole, which is unsustainable.

priorities.text: Wants to streamline regulation and encourage private capital investment so companies can raise wages, and attract more manufacturing and technology employers to the district.

positions.summary: Opposes removing legal barriers to entry and opposes extending government benefits to undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: we cannot afford to take down the existing legal barriers to entry into our nation and give undocumented arrivals generous benefits just for being here.

positions.summary: Opposes expanding the social safety net (more beneficiaries and higher payouts), which he says would worsen federal debt problems, and describes broader redistributive tax policy as "the politics of envy."
positions.quote: Increasing the social safety net to include both more beneficiaries and higher payouts will deepen these problems, not resolve them. We need fiscal discipline.
